blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Joint change detection and captioning seeks to localize changes and describe them from bi-temporal remote sensing images. A key challenge is translating dense visual evidence into the semantic conditions that guide description generation. We propose Explicit Semantic Anchors (ESA), a supervised interface that exposes entity presence, temporal appearance variation, and spatial extent. A prediction-guided readout combines visual features and predicted change probabilities, and three factor heads estimate the corresponding anchor activations. These activations guide generation through two complementary routes. The context route maps the three factor activations to three separate memory tokens, one per factor, and appends them to the dense visual memory, while the lexicon route produces an additive vocabulary bias at each decoding step. Dense visual memory remains available for spatial detail and information beyond the explicit factors. Anchor targets are derived from existing images and change annotations, requiring no additional anchor-level language annotation. At inference, all conditions are computed from the input image pair and the model's own predictions. Experiments on LEVIR-MCI and WHU-CDC show strong joint detection and captioning performance, supporting the use of supervised visual attributes as explicit conditions for change description generation.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
A change map and a change description offer complementary accounts of
how a scene evolves. In remote sensing, change detection (CD) localizes
changes at the pixel level, whereas change captioning (CC) expresses
their content in natural language. Multi-level change interpretation
(MCI) brings these tasks into a common framework [ 12 ] ,
combining spatially precise predictions with descriptions that people
can readily interpret. Realizing this complementarity requires more
than producing two outputs from the same image pair: the description
should be informed by the visual evidence underlying the change map.
This motivates a central question: how can a joint model turn
dense change evidence into explicit semantic conditions for language
generation?

blocks.en:
The challenge lies in the different decisions required by the two
tasks. Detection assigns labels to spatial locations, while captioning
selects a compact set of attributes and organizes them into a sentence.
Even a category-aware change map does not uniquely determine a
description. A caption may need to identify the affected entities,
interpret temporal appearance differences, and distinguish a localized
alteration from a more extensive transformation. Dense bi-temporal
features contain evidence for these decisions, but their presence in a
decoder’s visual memory does not expose which attributes have been
inferred or how they influence word selection. An explicit intermediate
representation would make part of this mapping available for direct
supervision and inspection.

blocks.en:
Recent work has strengthened the connection between visual perception
and language through shared representations and task interaction.
Joint models such as Change-Agent and ChangeMinds support detection and
captioning within a common architecture [ 12 , 21 ] .
LCCC introduces critique and correction between the two
tasks [ 10 ] , while CoDeRNet selectively transfers features
according to task-specific support and reliability
cues [ 6 ] . In change captioning, HiSem explores
hierarchical semantic organization [ 20 ] , and STAND
introduces semantic anchoring constraints [ 8 ] .
These approaches motivate a complementary question about the content
of semantic guidance: which attributes can be grounded in the
available visual supervision, and where should their predictions enter
the captioning process? We address this question through a supervised
interface between predicted change regions and language generation.

provides useful supervision for such an interface. Change masks

their categories. The ordered image pair provides appearance

annotations [ 23 ] . We use this available structure
to supervise intermediate visual attributes that can subsequently
condition a caption decoder. This reuses the existing images and masks
without requiring additional anchor-level language annotations.

blocks.en:
We propose Explicit Semantic Anchors (ESA) , an interface that
reads predicted change evidence and exposes three complementary
factors: entity presence , temporal appearance variation ,
and spatial extent . A shared visual pathway produces multi-scale
bi-temporal features and change probabilities. A prediction-guided
readout then combines global differences, category-conditioned
features, ordered temporal evidence, and region statistics. Three
supervised heads map this evidence to named factor states. Entity
states indicate which supported categories are present; temporal
states provide a weak appearance-polarity cue; and extent states
describe changed-area coverage. Their definitions make the predicted
conditions inspectable before decoding. The temporal factor is
supervised by intensity variation within changed regions, so it serves
as an appearance cue rather than a direct label for events such as
construction or demolition.

During training, auxiliary targets are derived from the existing
visual annotations and image attributes, whereas the anchor readout
always receives features and predicted change probabilities. At
inference, the image pair alone supplies the change map, anchor
activations, and autoregressively generated caption. Experiments on
LEVIR-MCI and WHU-CDC evaluate the resulting model through detection
accuracy, captioning metrics, and qualitative comparisons. They show
strong joint performance, with the relative advantages varying across
datasets and metrics.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are threefold: • We introduce an explicit semantic interface for MCI that
organizes prediction-guided visual evidence into supervised entity,
temporal-appearance, and spatial-extent factors, making these
intermediate conditions available for inspection. • We design a context route and a lexicon route that reuse the same anchor activations as three separate memory tokens and an additive vocabulary bias, connecting visual attributes to both contextual decoding and lexical selection. • We derive anchor supervision from existing images and change
annotations, enabling image-only inference without additional
anchor-level language annotation, and evaluate the framework on
two joint detection–captioning benchmarks.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Remote Sensing Change Captioning
blocks.zh: 2.1 遥感变化说明

blocks.en:
Remote sensing change captioning (CC) translates changes between bi-temporal images into natural-language descriptions.
A major line of research improves the encoding of temporal differences for language generation.
RSICCformer [ 13 ] introduced the LEVIR-CC benchmark and a dual-branch Transformer, while Chg2Cap [ 3 ] combines hierarchical attention with difference-aware feature refinement.
Beyond visual difference encoding, PromptCC [ 14 ] separates change-existence classification from caption generation and connects visual representations to a pretrained language model through multiple prompts.
HiSem [ 20 ] further organizes change semantics through discrepancy-aware interaction, image-level routing, and token-level mixture-of-experts modeling.
blocks.zh:
遥感变化标题(CC)将双时段图像之间的变化转化为自然语言描述.
主要的研究线改进了语言生成时差的编码.
RSICCFormer [13]引入了LEVIR-CC基准和双分支变换器,而Chg2Cap [3]结合了等级关注和差别感知特征的完善.
除了视觉差异编码外,PowerCC [14] 将变化存在分类从标题生成中分离出来,并通过多个提示将视觉表现与预先训练的语言模型连接起来.
HiSem [20] 通过差异感知交互,图像级路由,以及符号级混合专家模型化,进一步组织变化语义.

blocks.en:
Another line strengthens the spatial or semantic evidence used for description.
MaskApproxNet [ 17 ] estimates change masks through conditional diffusion and applies frequency-guided feature fusion before autoregressive caption decoding.
For building-damage captioning, KGBDCNet [ 19 ] combines keyword-guided cross-modal retrieval with spatiotemporal feature modeling to emphasize damage-related content.
These approaches illustrate how change recognition, spatial cues, and semantic guidance support caption generation.
CC evaluates change understanding through language. Joint MCI additionally requires explicit spatial predictions and evaluation of both outputs.
blocks.zh:
另一行加强了用于描述的空间或语义证据.
MaskApproxNet [17] 估计通过有条件的传播来改变口罩,并在自动回转标题解码前应用频率导特性聚变.
对于建筑损坏标题,KGBDCNet [19] 将关键词制导的跨模式检索与spatiopal特征模型结合起来,以强调与损害有关的内容。
这些方法说明了变化识别、空间提示和语义指导如何支持标题生成。
CC评价通过语言改变理解. 联合多指标类集倡议还要求对两种产出进行明确的空间预测和评价。

blocks.en: 2.2 Remote Sensing Change Detection
blocks.zh: 2.2 遥感变化探测

blocks.en:
Remote sensing change detection (CD) predicts spatially explicit changes from multi-temporal imagery.
Early fully convolutional Siamese networks [ 7 ] fuse features from shared-weight temporal encoders through concatenation or absolute differences in skip connections.
To incorporate broader context, BIT [ 4 ] models interactions among compact semantic tokens and projects their context back to dense image features.
ChangeFormer [ 1 ] instead combines a hierarchical Siamese Transformer encoder with an MLP decoder for multiscale change prediction.
Extending this architectural progression, ChangeMamba [ 5 ] introduces spatiotemporal state-space modeling for binary and semantic change detection as well as building damage assessment.
blocks.zh:
遥感变化探测(CD)从多时段图像中预测空间明显的变化.
早点全面革命 暹罗网络[7] 引信特性来自共享重量的时空编码器,通过协和或跳过连接的绝对差异.
为了纳入更广泛的背景,BIT[4]模型在紧凑语义符号之间的相互作用,并预测其背景回到密集的图像特征.
ChangeFormer [1] 转而将一个层次分明的暹罗变形器编码器与MLP解码器结合,用于多尺度变化预测.
ChangeMamba[5] 扩展了这种建筑进步,引入了用于二进制和语义变化探测以及建筑损害评估的spatiotemporal状态-空间模型。

blocks.en:
Recent work also expands the semantic scope of detection.
OpenDPR [ 9 ] addresses open-vocabulary CD by combining foundation-model change proposals with diffusion-guided visual prototype retrieval for category identification.
Thus, CD encompasses both change localization and structured semantic prediction, including change categories or damage levels.
These structured outputs complement the natural-language descriptions targeted by CC.
blocks.zh:
最近的工作也扩大了检测的语义范围.
OpenDPR [9]通过将基础模型更改建议与传播引导的视觉原型检索相结合,用于类别识别,从而解决了开放-vocabulary CD.
因此,CD既包括变化本地化,也包括结构化的语义预测,包括变化类别或损害水平.
这些结构化产出补充了CC针对的自然语言描述.

blocks.en: 2.3 Multi-Level Change Interpretation
blocks.zh: 2.3 多层次变化解释

blocks.en: Multi-level change interpretation (MCI) unifies CD and CC to jointly predict pixel-level change maps and semantic descriptions. Change-Agent [ 12 ] introduced LEVIR-MCI and a joint perception model with bi-temporal iterative interaction, while CTMTNet [ 16 ] provided the LEVIR-CDC and WHU-CDC datasets through attention-based enhancement and bi-temporal fusion. Building on these formulations, ChangeMinds [ 21 ] uses ChangeLSTM and a unified decoder to serve both heads, and Semantic-CC [ 24 ] employs a SAM-based encoder with pixel-level guidance coordinated through a three-stage training strategy, connecting language generation to spatially grounded representations. Recent methods further address this coupling with distinct mechanisms. Change-UP [ 22 ] integrates adaptive representations and text-driven style diversification, LCCC [ 10 ] couples detection-derived change tokens with a critique–correction framework, and CoDeRNet [ 6 ] selectively routes features based on receiver-side support needs and sender-side reliability cues. A central issue across these designs is how to exchange complementary task evidence while preserving the spatial detail required by CD and the semantic selectivity required by CC.

Change-Agent [12]引入了LEVIR-MCI和具有双时段迭代相互作用的联合感知模型,而CTMTNet [16]通过基于注意力的增强和双时段聚变提供了LEVIR-CDC和WHU-CDC数据集. 基于这些配方,ChangingMinds[21]使用ChangleLSTM和一个统一的解码器为双头服务,Semantic-CC[24]使用一个基于SAM的编码器,通过三阶段培训战略协调像素级指导,将语言生成与空间定位的表示连接起来. 最近的方法进一步处理这种与不同机制的结合。 变革-UP[22] 将适应性表述和文字驱动的风格多样化、LCCC[10]夫妇检测-衍生的改变符号与批评-校正框架相结合,以及CoDeRNet[6]基于接收方支持需要和发送方可靠性提示的选择性路线特征。 在整个设计过程中,一个核心问题是如何交换补充性任务证据,同时保留CD所要求的空间细节和CC所要求的语义选择性。

blocks.en: Figure 2 compares predicted maps and generated descriptions with LCCC and CoDeRNet. In the first example, ESA describes the group of houses built along the roads, capturing the principal changed entity and its spatial arrangement. This description is similar to CoDeRNet’s and does not include every detail in the reference, such as the additional villas at the bottom. The corresponding detection map identifies the repeated building footprints and the road-change region. In the second example, ESA focuses on the newly appearing road at the bottom of the scene, while the magnified crops permit a closer comparison of the thin road segment and its junction. These cases illustrate how the map and sentence provide complementary accounts of the same change.

blocks.en: The building examples expose differences in foreground coverage and boundary shape. In the last example, ESA describes a large building together with a parking lot, and the predicted map delineates the main building-change regions. Such examples support inspection of entity selection, spatial wording, and localization together; they do not establish that every generated attribute is correct. In particular, the global anchor factors do not explicitly assign an event or a count to each object, and the dense visual memory remains necessary for finer spatial and contextual details.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We presented Explicit Semantic Anchors (ESA) for joint remote sensing change detection and captioning. ESA reads features and predicted change regions through a supervised interface that exposes entity presence, temporal appearance variation, and spatial extent. Retaining dense visual memory allows the decoder to combine these explicit conditions with detailed scene evidence. Results on LEVIR-MCI and WHU-CDC demonstrate strong joint performance and support the value of exposing visual attributes to the caption decoder. Entity semantics follow the detection ontology, the temporal target is a weak photometric proxy, and extent measures area coverage rather than individual object change. Future work can extend this interface to object level event representations and evaluate the grounding of individual generated claims, building on ESA’s central principle of exposing and reusing supervised visual evidence within language generation.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍了用于联合遥感变化探测和标题的明晰语义控制器(欧空局)。 欧空局通过一个可显示实体存在、时间外观变化和空间范围的有监督的界面来阅读特征和预测变化区域。 保留密集的视觉内存可以使解码器将这些明确的条件与详细的场景证据结合起来. LEVIR-MCI和WHU-CDC的结果显示了强大的联合性能,并支持将视觉属性暴露于标题解码器的价值. 实体语义学遵循检测本体论,时间目标是一种弱的光度测量代词,范围测量范围覆盖而不是单个物体变化. 今后的工作可以扩大这一接口,使之包括物体级事件说明,并评价个人产生的索赔的理由,以欧空局的核心原则为基础,即在语言生成过程中揭露和重新使用受监督的视觉证据。
